name: Furen's Armor
summary: In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard seeks help testing new armor. An aspiring warrior gathers spider fangs, chimaera horns, and phlogiston so the master smith can forge fire-hardened mail. Furen gives the finished armor to the warrior and promises to share what he learned with Alliance smiths.

sections.title: A Master's Breakthrough
sections.body: Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorer in Stormwind, works to improve how Alliance armor withstands heat and crushing blows. He asks an aspiring warrior to gather rare materials for his tests. The resulting mail proves a success and strengthens Furen's standing among Alliance armorers.

sections.title: Sharing the Craft
sections.body: Furen gives the finished fire-hardened mail to the warrior who gathered the materials, grateful for their help. The experiments also deepen his knowledge of protective smithing. He plans to send his notes and findings to other Alliance smiths, so they can put the new methods to use.

faq.answer: Furen Longbeard is a master dwarven armorer in Stormwind who works extensively with the Alliance's martial orders, especially warriors seeking specialized armor.

faq.q: What kind of armor did Furen create?
faq.answer: Furen forged a Fire Hardened Hauberk, a mail chest piece made with rare fangs, horns, and phlogiston. It is designed to withstand fierce attacks and extreme heat.

faq.q: Where does Furen Longbeard send his smithing discoveries?
faq.answer: Furen promises to send his findings and notes to fellow blacksmiths across the Alliance, sharing the tested tempering methods with forges throughout the realm.

faq.q: Why was the warrior asked to gather reagents for Furen?
faq.answer: Furen needed rare, volatile materials to test new smithing techniques. Unable to leave his forge to hunt spiders in the Wetlands and chimaeras in Stonetalon, he relied on an ambitious warrior to gather them.

faq.q: Where is this armor forged and delivered?
faq.answer: Furen forges and delivers the armor at his forge in Stormwind, where he completes the mail suit.

faq.q: Does this work benefit other Alliance fighters?
faq.answer: Yes. Furen plans to share what he learned with other Alliance armorers, hoping they will use the methods to make strong equipment for Alliance soldiers.

angles.text: As an Alliance warrior, earning Furen's custom-tempered armor marks a passage into frontline service and offers protection for early campaigns.
Furen's experiment reflects how Alliance smiths share metallurgical findings to improve their craft in Stormwind and Ironforge.
Strong arms help keep Alliance forces alive against threats from the Defias, gnolls, and hostile elemental forces.
